title: Entry context selects local versus carried scope for an ordered payload
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. A productive ordered payload is interpreted under a binary scope selector derived from entry context: LOCAL applies its arguments only to the current clause, while CARRY permits a later compatible clause to update the active payload without repeating every argument. This is a scope hypothesis, not participant identity continuity and not a whole-form glossary.

observations: GDT282 finds opaque wrapper identity transfer across registers, but no lexical meaning; the present card uses only the transferable context signal.
GDT286 tests host-to-wrapper conditioning and reports a host/context effect without an accepted semantic endpoint; host times position is not treated as a solved meaning rule.
GDT318 reports a compact formal selector from line-start and preceding-DY state, with no semantic interpretation.
GDT563 carries active action/argument structure in a formal microphrase renderer, while GDT608 shows that exact whole-form residuals remain necessary.

mechanism.frame: Each clause has an ordered productive payload P(op,args,residual). A deterministic context function SCOPE(entry_context, wrapper_state) returns exactly LOCAL or CARRY before the payload is reduced.
rules: LOCAL consumes all arguments in the current clause and closes the payload at the clause boundary.
CARRY leaves one typed active payload slot open; the next compatible payload may update that slot, but an incompatible entry or explicit reset closes it.
The whole-form residual identifies the occurrence and may distinguish payload variants, but it cannot invent a participant or bypass the scope selector.
chain: Clause 1 establishes active payload P1 with an explicit argument under CARRY.
Clause 2 presents a compatible ordered form with one changed argument; CARRY updates P1 to P2 without silently creating a new event.
Clause 3 begins under LOCAL or an explicit reset, so its same-looking payload applies only to clause 3 and cannot alter P2.
rivals: ALWAYS_LOCAL closes every payload after each clause.
ALWAYS_CARRY lets every compatible later form mutate the prior payload until an arbitrary analyst reset.

design.complete_reading_consequence: For a complete multi-clause passage with a fixed entry-context pattern, the model predicts exactly one carried update between the first two compatible forms and no leakage into the later reset/local clause. ALWAYS_LOCAL predicts two independent payloads; ALWAYS_CARRY predicts a mutation of the final clause as well. The contrast concerns scope and update count, not an assumed identity for the participants.
design.falsifier: Predeclare a complete passage with two compatible ordered payloads followed by a context change or explicit boundary. Reject the scoped model if the same entry context yields both LOCAL and CARRY without a written trigger, if an update crosses a declared reset, or if a carried slot has no typed source argument. Reject ALWAYS_LOCAL only if an independently repeated argument is omitted while the later form demonstrably updates the earlier operation; reject ALWAYS_CARRY if the reset clause demonstrably leaves the earlier payload unchanged.
design.strongest_failure: GDT282/286/318/563 establish compressible formal context and state carry, not semantic scope. A wrapper or preceding-DY selector may be purely orthographic; without an independently observed boundary or omitted argument, LOCAL and CARRY remain observationally equivalent.

predecessors.limit: Opaque wrapper transfer only; no semantic payload scope.
Host/context conditioning is formal and did not pass the host-position semantic gate.
Entry-state compression only; no meaning or reset semantics.
Formal active action/argument carry in a renderer, not an independently bound target operation.
Wrapper-scoped participant continuity; this card leaves participant identity opaque and varies only local-versus-carried payload scope.

dependencies: A finite predeclared entry-context selector and exact reset/boundary rule are required before fitting.
At least one complete passage must contain a compatible later payload with an omitted or changed argument and an independently visible context change.
Repeated spelling is not enough to identify the same participant or physical referent; active slots remain typed variables.
No target word gloss, Latin default, arbitrary nearest-reference rule, or post hoc reset is permitted.
design.access: Retained GDT282/286/318/563/608 reports and bounded duplicate checks only; no target data/image, reserve, GDT1001, source packet, decoder, experiment, route, ledger, or push.
